current.text: He is back from a torn Achilles suffered on January 31. Experts expect him to start the season without a minutes limit.
Yahoo lists him as questionable with a toe injury.
He is expected to start for the Pelicans next to Trey Murphy and Zion Williamson. Jeremiah Fears is the other guard pushing for minutes.
Minutes are the main risk, not health. The Pelicans roster is crowded. If he plays less than 33 minutes, or the team puts Fears first, his value drops.
One expert projects him at about 25 percent usage and 33 minutes, and expects more minutes and better shooting than last season.
Experts call him the best fantasy target on the Pelicans and expect a top 50 finish, not top 30.
Experts call him undervalued at an ADP around 70 and a favorite sleeper. In recent mocks they took him at picks 41 to 47 and in round 4, and they were happy with those picks.
In an expert auction mock he went for 24 USD. The bidder who wanted him hoped to pay 15 to 16 USD and stopped at 23 USD.
Last season he turned 70 percent of his deflections into steals. If that rate falls back, more minutes may not raise his steals.
The Pelicans have a league-high 16 back-to-backs. One expert does not expect him to sit back-to-backs.
With a season ending March 28, the Pelicans play 4, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks. Experts call that a good schedule.
The Pelicans have a new coach, Jamahl Mosley, who brings a defense-first identity. Experts project a weak team of about 34 wins near the bottom of the West.

durable.text: He has been a good steals player over his career and could average two steals.
His free throw shooting is excellent.
He is not a good three-point shooter. He can make threes but does not space the floor.
He turns the ball over far more than the player pool, which is his clear weak category.
He blocks few shots for a good guard defender. His contest-to-block rate last season was below his career rate, so a small rise is possible.
He tore his Achilles on January 31.
